findings.title: $__range guard is evaluated after interpolation
findings.body: runSplitQuery now interpolates each target before calling `partition(...)`/`querySupportsSplitting`, but `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to keep `$__range` queries out of time splitting. Once `applyTemplateVariables` has run, `$__range` has already been substituted (with the full request range), so the check no longer sees the placeholder and those queries are split anyway. The code’s own comment states these queries must not be split because each split uses a different time range; replacing the variable once at the start and then splitting can therefore produce incorrect results. The predicate should be evaluated against the original target expression before interpolation (or the raw flag should be carried through), with a regression test for a `$__range` query.

findings.title: Targets are interpolated twice in shard splitting
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates every target here, then `splitQueriesByStreamShard` calls `runSplitQuery`, which now also interpolates all targets. The shard test was updated to expect `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times for a single original target, confirming the double pass. Template interpolation is not guaranteed to be idempotent: variable values containing `$`/variable syntax can be expanded a second time, and any non-idempotent rewriting is applied twice after the shard selector has already been injected. Interpolation should happen at one entry point only: either pass already-interpolated targets to a non-interpolating `runSplitQuery` variant, or move interpolation up so shard splitting does not pre-interpolate before calling it.
